notes: All currency amounts are absolute values (not millions). Historical EBIT uses GAAP operating income.

NWC construction (applied consistently in history and used to derive NWC % of sales): (Total current assets − cash and short-term investments) − (Total current liabilities − current maturities of long-term debt). Contract liabilities are included in operating working capital (common in DCF models but may differ from some practitioner conventions).

Forecast driver inputs are base-case assumptions (not management guidance for out-years). 2026 capex is kept consistent with the company’s $110m to $120m range by using capex % sales derived from the modeled 2026 revenue. ([s205.q4cdn.com](https://s205.q4cdn.com/557255526/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/Webcast-Slides-Q4-2025.pdf))

Comps EV/NTM revenue and EV/NTM EBITDA are approximated using StockAnalysis EV/Sales and EV/EBITDA ratios; StockAnalysis does not explicitly label these as NTM in the accessible view, so they are treated as NTM proxies for the purpose of reasonableness checks (gap noted). ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/cdw/statistics/))

Tax rate is modeled as 0.26 based on the company’s non-GAAP effective tax rate guide range (25.5% to 26.5%) rather than strictly using the single-year effective tax rate. ([s205.q4cdn.com](https://s205.q4cdn.com/557255526/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/Webcast-Slides-Q4-2025.pdf))

NOL utilization % is assumed (0.80) because the filing discloses NOL balances but does not provide a complete valuation utilization schedule suitable for this specific DCF input package. ([s205.q4cdn.com](https://s205.q4cdn.com/557255526/files/doc_downloads/2026/02/CDW-2025-12-31-10K.pdf))

catalysts: Evidence of sustained gross profit growth and operating leverage through 2026 quarters (supporting mid-single-digit earnings growth). ([s205.q4cdn.com](https://s205.q4cdn.com/557255526/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/Webcast-Slides-Q4-2025.pdf))

Capital allocation execution (dividend growth and potential buybacks) contingent on net leverage trends and free cash flow generation. ([s205.q4cdn.com](https://s205.q4cdn.com/557255526/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/Webcast-Slides-Q4-2025.pdf))
M&A and mix shifts into higher-margin software/services solutions could move margins above the base case.
company_overview: CDW is a multi-brand provider of information technology (IT) solutions across the IT lifecycle. ([multiples.vc](https://multiples.vc/public-comps/cdw-valuation-multiples))

Service offerings span hardware, software, and integrated IT services (including hybrid infrastructure, digital experience, and security). ([multiples.vc](https://multiples.vc/public-comps/cdw-valuation-multiples))

Operates across the United States, the United Kingdom, and Canada, with reportable segments including Corporate, Small Business, Public, and Other. ([multiples.vc](https://multiples.vc/public-comps/cdw-valuation-multiples))
current_context: Full-year 2025 results: net sales $22,424.1m (+6.8% YoY) and operating income $1,655.6m; effective tax rate ~25.3%. ([s205.q4cdn.com](https://s205.q4cdn.com/557255526/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/CDW-2025-12-31-Earnings-Release.pdf))

2026 outlook: customer spend driven by U.S. IT growth plus a premium target of ~200 to 300 bps; gross profit expected to grow low single digits; non-GAAP EPS expected to grow mid single digits. ([s205.q4cdn.com](https://s205.q4cdn.com/557255526/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/Webcast-Slides-Q4-2025.pdf))

2026 guideposts: annual interest expense net $225m to $230m; non-GAAP effective tax rate 25.5% to 26.5%; capex $110m to $120m. ([s205.q4cdn.com](https://s205.q4cdn.com/557255526/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/Webcast-Slides-Q4-2025.pdf))
investment_highlights: Base-case revenue growth reflects a mid-single-digit 2026 start that gradually normalizes, consistent with management’s customer spend premium framework. ([s205.q4cdn.com](https://s205.q4cdn.com/557255526/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/Webcast-Slides-Q4-2025.pdf))
Base-case EBIT margin expands from the 2025 level as gross profit grows low single digits and operating leverage is preserved (margin ramps to ~7.75% by 2030).

Reinvestment profile stays close to recent history and 2026 capex guidance (modeled as ~0.49% of sales in the out-years). ([s205.q4cdn.com](https://s205.q4cdn.com/557255526/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/Webcast-Slides-Q4-2025.pdf))
Working-capital intensity normalizes over time (modeled NWC % of sales trending down from the 2025 level).

Tax headwind is mitigated by existing net operating loss carryforwards (NOLs reported $108m; utilization modeled as an assumption). ([s205.q4cdn.com](https://s205.q4cdn.com/557255526/files/doc_downloads/2026/02/CDW-2025-12-31-10K.pdf))
key_risks: IT spending slowdowns or delayed customer purchasing could reduce revenue growth below base-case levels.
Margin compression driven by competitive pricing, services mix shifts, or higher operating costs.
Working-capital deterioration (higher NWC % of sales) reducing free cash flow conversion.

Leverage/interest-rate sensitivity given the company’s debt profile and net interest expense guidance. ([s205.q4cdn.com](https://s205.q4cdn.com/557255526/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/Webcast-Slides-Q4-2025.pdf))

valuation_summary: DCF base case uses historical operating economics (EBIT margin, D&A, capex) and overlays management’s 2026 guideposts (tax, interest, capex) to keep assumptions grounded. ([s205.q4cdn.com](https://s205.q4cdn.com/557255526/files/doc_downloads/2026/02/CDW-2025-12-31-10K.pdf))

Discount rate uses a market-derived WACC (~7.94%) and a terminal growth rate of 3.0%, consistent with a mature North American distributor profile. ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/cdw/statistics/))
Peer comps provide a reasonableness check using forward P/E and EV/EBITDA / EV/Sales multiples as proxies for NTM valuation ranges (data availability constraint noted).
